note: Grounded defect list from outputs/arduino_kit_run_v2 (formed from the four documents and the runtime code, then cross-checked against the QA report read last). The QA report independently reached the same root cause; two defects below (D2, D5) are ones I found in code that the QA report does not name.
defects: D1 SYSTEMIC RENDERING: all four documents (L01-L04) emit eight sections (Engage/Explore/Explain/Elaborate/Evaluate/Identification/Troubleshooting/Adult safety verification) as literal pretty-printed JSON instead of prose. Not four failures - one templating bug reaching every unit.

D2 ROOT CAUSE IN CODE (not named in QA report): runtime/session_bridge.py:207-215 _markdown() calls json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) for each 5E section. The emitter never had a prose renderer for those fields; the title, job sentence and objectives DO render as prose, which is why the failure is invisible to any check looking at the head of the file.

D3 SCHEMA VALIDITY PASSED ANYWAY: results/unit_checks.json records LAB-SCHEMA-VALID=PASS, DOMAIN-SCHEMA-VALID=PASS, DOMAIN-VERIFIER=PASS, RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES=PASS on every unit. The upstream lab.json was well-formed; the defect is entirely downstream of schema validation, so no schema check could have seen it.

D4 GATE-2 TEXT CHECKS INERT: no TEXT-READABILITY-BAND or TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS result exists for any unit, though prompt.md:193-195 names both as mandatory. A readability metric run on a JSON dump would have failed loudly - the cheapest available canary was not running.

D5 RENDER CHECK TOO WEAK (not named in QA report): the only check on the rendered artifact is runtime/checks.py:82 rasterize_and_check_nonblank, which rasterizes each PDF page and fails only if a page is near-uniform (extrema[1]-extrema[0] <= 2). A page of pretty-printed JSON is dense black-on-white and passes trivially. policy/controller.v1.yaml lists a PDF_VISUAL_QA state but no PDF_VISUAL_QA verdict artifact exists in the run.

D6 SOLE SUBJECTIVE READER BYPASSED: acceptance.json on all four units records routing_divergence=USER_AUTHORIZED_IN_SESSION_MODEL; cross-family judge bypassed. The only reviewer that reads output the way a human would never ran.
D7 VOCAB CAP: QA report High finding - L04 introduces mAVohm, 10A socket, mode dial, fuse against a 2-new-term cap.
note2: Threads 1 and 2 are deliberately separate: the user's question is precisely whether validating the rendered document is a different job from validating the upstream schema, and D3 shows empirically that it is.

claim: Schema-valid LLM output can still be semantically wrong; structured output is an interface layer, not a substitute for downstream verification
result: VERIFIED - abstract retrieved. Yin Li, 'When JSON Is Not Enough: Semantic Reliability of Schema-Constrained LLM Ordering Agents'. Abstract states 'schema-valid output can still have large semantic error rates'; strongest model reaches '100% schema validity, yet semantic success remains near 80%'; weaker models show 'schema-valid unsafe acceptances ... in double digits'; concludes 'structured output is a necessary interface layer, not a substitute for domain verification and fail-closed execution'. SCOPE NOTE: the domain is ordering/transaction agents, NOT document rendering - cite it for the validity-vs-semantics principle only, never as evidence about rendering.
decision: keep, cite in schema_validity_vs_semantic_quality thread; do not overclaim to rendering

claim: Benchmarks that measure only schema compliance miss value-level correctness; near-perfect schema compliance coexists with much lower value accuracy
result: VERIFIED - abstract retrieved. Structured Output Benchmark (SOB). Abstract: existing benchmarks 'focus on schema compliance alone'; 'models achieve near-perfect schema compliance, yet the best Value Accuracy, measured by exact leaf-value match, reaches only 83.0% on text, 67.2% on images, and 23.7% on audio'. SCOPE NOTE: this is about extraction value accuracy, not about rendering structured data into prose.
decision: keep, cite in schema_validity_vs_semantic_quality thread for the measurement-gap claim only

claim: Current practice puts format/structure/schema conformance in deterministic code checks and reserves LLM judges for subjective dimensions

Separating deterministic checks from LLM-based scoring improves reliability'. Vendor article, but primary about its own recommended eval stack.
